newsitem.title: FRANCE: SocGen sets up private pension fund firm.
newsitem.headline: SocGen sets up private pension fund firm.

text.p: French bank Societe Generale said on Monday it was setting up a life insurance firm Sogeretraite to specialise in management of private pensions which will be allowed in France under a draft adopted last week.

Societe Generale said it would offer pre-packaged schemes of various types including monetary funds and funds investing 100 percent in shares and schemes which employees could adhere to in the absence of a fund agreement at the level of their company.
Sogeretraite would also offer tailored plans for large firms managed along the lines of Anglo-Saxon pension funds, it said in a statement.

Rival bank BNP announced on February 4 that it was setting up a pension fund management firm called Natio-Retraite and hoped to take five percent of a market which could total 20-25 billion francs a year within three or four years.

After adoption of the private pensions bill last week, the bill's author Jean-Pierre Thomas said he expected that the decrees applying the law would be in place in time to allow the first pension funds to start operating in the autumn.
